title: Pele Diagrams in Grove
summary: Native image presentation chosen: replace the renderer behind Mermaid fences after proving bounded JavaScript execution, SVG styles and font measurements. Preserve source fallback and host typography.

sources.text: Let's plan on moving from mermaid to https://pele.run/

https://pele.run/ — JavaScript render/mount API, Mermaid syntax compatibility, CSS-variable theming and security documentation. Compatibility is an upstream claim, not Grove verification. Pele changes layout; arbitrary Mermaid HTML labels do not carry over.

src/views/mermaid.rs:47 extension, :58 parser, :108 render/cache, :205 theme, :260 rasterizer; src/views/inline_html.rs:539 registration. Cargo.toml:206 pins mermaid-rs-renderer. No portable embedded JS runtime is directly integrated; Cargo.lock javascriptcore-rs belongs to the WebKit stack.

src/platform/inline_html.rs:90 document creation, :142 report height, :157 theme scripts; src/views/inline_html.rs:35 CSP forbids workers; :258 prepends policy. DESIGN.md:15 fonts, :17 zoom and :172 document lifecycle.

claims.text: Mermaid fences display Pele diagrams after rendering succeeds.
claims.detail: Native image presentation is settled by the user. Keep existing GPUI scrolling, transcript placement, accessible image description and source identity. Pele geometry will differ; theme changes rerender rather than use live browser CSS.

children.text: While streaming or rendering: selectable Mermaid code with ordinary Copy behavior
After success: Pele diagram within the existing transcript image well
Existing Mermaid source remains the document format.
children.detail: src/views/mermaid.rs:58–107 keeps case-insensitive mermaid fences, matching closed backtick/tilde fences and resource prechecks. src/views/inline_html.rs:539 keeps the extension attached to shared Markdown. Do not require Pele-specific fences or mutate saved messages.

entries.title: Preserve the parser
entries.detail: Only closed, nonempty, bounded fences become render candidates; incomplete streaming blocks stay source.

entries.title: Check real compatibility
entries.detail: Build representative corpus from current tests plus Mermaid 12.1 builtin families claimed by Pele; check syntax directives, labels and errors. Unsupported or rejected inputs stay source.

entries.title: Preserve authored layout intent
entries.detail: Keep explicit LR/TB etc.; no host autoDirection override. Review Pele layout changes rather than compare exact old coordinates.

claims.text: Dependency removal waits for a working, bounded Pele adapter.
claims.detail: This is a migration gate, not an assertion that a JS library drops into Rust. Keep mermaid-rs-renderer until the selected route renders the corpus and meets host safety/lifecycle limits. If the gate fails, report evidence and revise the architecture with the user before removal.

entries.title: Pin and audit the actual JS distribution
entries.detail: Confirm license, bundle format, transitive dependencies and required globals; vendor a reproducible offline bundle with version/hash and provenance. Do not assume browser APIs or npm runtime availability.

entries.title: Prove the selected execution route
entries.detail: Native: evaluate runtime candidates on every target; prove Pele render, text measurement, bounded memory and interruptible execution without DOM/network/file globals. Browser: prove trusted offline script, resource limits, lifecycle and isolated execution.

entries.title: Prove native SVG rendering if selected
entries.detail: Materialize Pele CSS variables/currentColor and required styles into bounded SVG using a host palette; use bundled DM Sans metrics matching rasterization. Reject unresolved style/HTML constructs. Prove real resvg output for labels, markers and diagrams.

entries.title: Stop and replan on a failed gate
entries.detail: If JS globals, font metrics, CSS resolution, interruptibility or platform packaging fail, compare a browser-owned SVG route versus isolated helper rendering with evidence. Do not silently weaken safety or replace the dependency anyway.

children.text: Existing document hosts do not provide an SVG export pipeline.
children.detail: src/platform/inline_html.rs:142 returns bounded height and :157 applies scripts, not SVG data. Existing hosts run on the UI thread. A browser-to-native SVG export path requires new bounded transport and asynchronous ownership; it is not a free reuse.

children.text: Browser presentation requires a separate isolation and lifecycle proof.
children.detail: src/views/inline_html.rs:35 currently sets worker-src none; do not claim a main-thread timeout can interrupt synchronous renderer work. If choosing browser SVG, prove a narrowly scoped trusted worker/helper policy and termination, SVG delivery, text measurements and cross-platform support without weakening ordinary authored HTML policy.

entries.title: Exercise many diagram documents
entries.detail: Test transcript virtualization, multiple diagrams, clip/scroll, session switch, collapsed rows, window changes and teardown against NativeDocument leases.

entries.title: Prove browser resource bounds
entries.detail: Measure view count and memory; bound active document/cache/pending work and host scalar/SVG responses. Browser responsive sizing must not oscillate report height.

entries.title: Prove actual cancellation
entries.detail: Terminate isolated rendering at deadline, recover capacity, and keep source visible. A 30-second load polling timeout does not prove synchronous JS interruption.

claims.text: Incomplete, invalid and unsafe diagrams keep copyable source.
claims.detail: Retain the current source-first lifecycle. Rendering completion must target the original source/theme revision, not a replacement session or newer input. Preserve the Image role and Mermaid source description in the image route.

transitions.label: Matching closing fence and limits pass
Bounded valid result for matching revision
Parse, execution, SVG, timeout or policy failure
Host theme changes; rerender image route

children.text: Rendering preserves resource limits and denies external content.
children.detail: src/views/mermaid.rs:17–21 remains the baseline: 8 KiB source, 100 statements/structural markers, 2048 maximum raster side, 24 cache entries and two pending renders. Add explicit JS execution deadline, memory/SVG output limits and structural complexity validation; choose concrete thresholds from measured corpus before rollout.

entries.title: Treat Mermaid source strictly as data
entries.detail: Serialize input through the runtime API, never interpolate it into executable script/HTML. Disable Pele links, image references and unsafe source config overrides; inspect actual release options.

entries.title: Retain the rasterizer deny policy
entries.detail: src/views/mermaid.rs:275–280 blocks network, file and data-image resolution. Keep both image href resolvers returning None; reject script/event/foreignObject content before browser insertion if applicable.

entries.title: Contain failures and release capacity
entries.detail: Distinguish Pending/Ready/Failed; release slots after errors/cancellation. Enforce an interruptible deadline rather than only panic catching. Cache by source, theme and renderer/bundle options; invalidate correctly.

claims.text: Diagrams follow Grove fonts, palette and app zoom.
claims.detail: Use DESIGN.md:15–17, src/theme.rs and src/views/tokens.rs as authority. Maintain DM Sans with platform glyph fallback, semantic text/surface/border colors and exactly-once rem scaling. Keep the current source direction and diagram well styling.

entries.title: Map host colors to Pele theme tokens
entries.detail: Native route snapshots theme values and resolves CSS before resvg; browser route updates trusted CSS in place. Do not let diagram source replace host fonts or enable external resources.

entries.title: Match measurements to actual bundled fonts
entries.detail: src/views/mermaid.rs:264–274 already loads DM Sans into resvg. Prove equivalent JS layout metrics, multiline and Unicode fallback; mismatches block the gate.

entries.title: Check physical output at host zoom
entries.detail: Test default and changed rem size, narrow/wide transcript, display scale changes and palette changes within one appearance. Preserve raster cap and ensure labels do not clip or scale twice.

claims.text: Delivery requires native and provider-specific acceptance evidence.
claims.detail: Future implementation only: run relevant renderer/parser tests, formatting and conformance checks; inspect an isolated current native build before final installation. Run ./install.sh once after final changes at the selected delivery endpoint, unless the user overrides. No release is authorized.

entries.title: Run focused checks and read raw output
entries.detail: Use repo-established cargo fmt --check, renderer/parser unit tests, clippy/conformance recipes applicable to changed files. Include actual Pele corpus, failure/timeout recovery and denied href tests, not only mocks.

entries.title: Inspect the real native view
entries.detail: Capture screenshots and interaction results for normal/narrow width, zoom, theme, Unicode, many diagrams, copy fallback, invalid/oversized input, streaming, scroll and session changes. Record exact build and platform.

entries.title: Codex: untested; live verification planned
entries.detail: Stream a real Codex response containing Mermaid, observe open-fence source, closure, rendering, Copy and fallback. Fixtures only prove the renderer/parser boundary.

entries.title: Claude: untested; live verification planned
entries.detail: Repeat through the live Claude response boundary; do not infer provider parity from Codex or shared fixtures.

entries.title: macOS / Linux / Windows: untested; checks planned
entries.detail: Verify selected runtime/bundle packaging and native font/theme/zoom behavior on all three. Browser route additionally needs actual view focus/scroll/worker lifecycle tests per backend. Mark unavailable platforms untested with reason, never verified by source inspection.

scope: Plan only: no production implementation, build, tests or installation performed. Native Review response / Send response records feedback and does not authorize implementation.

Estimated six-file baseline: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/views/mermaid.rs, a new isolated Pele adapter, vendored pinned JS asset and provenance. Exact files/counts follow the feasibility spike; src/views/conformance.rs changes only if affected checks require it. Browser route adds document integration and platform review.

Future implementation retains mermaid fence syntax and current source fallback. No CDN/runtime package download, external image resolution, clickable diagram actions or general HTML sandbox relaxation.

Existing parser source budgets remain unless evidence warrants a separately reviewed change. Keep source-declared direction; responsive automatic direction and new pan/zoom controls are outside this migration.
Update DESIGN.md only if the approved presentation introduces an invariant; update grove-ui skill only if its verification procedure changes.
Native images are selected. Browser SVG is only a contingency requiring replanning if the feasibility gate fails, not an active implementation option.
